chunks: And regarding the palm: if it breaks and is set without deformity or defect, its wergild is one-fifth of the wergild of the hand, being one hundred Dinars; and if the palm is disjointed, its wergild is one-third of the wergild of the hand, being one hundred and sixty-six Dinars and two-thirds of a Dinar; and regarding its exposure, it is a quarter of the wergild of its breaking, being twenty-five Dinars; and the wergild for the displacement of its bones is fifty Dinars, being half the wergild for its breaking; and regarding its piercing, if it is not sealed up, it is one-fifth of the wergild of the hand, being one hundred Dinars. So if it was pierced (and sealed), its wergild is a quarter of the wergild of its breaking, being twenty-five Dinars.

And regarding the wergild of the fingers and the bones which are in the palm: so regarding the thumb when it is cut off, it is one-third of the wergild of the hand, being one hundred and sixty-six Dinars and two-thirds of a Dinar; and the wergild of the bone of the thumb which is in the palm, if set without deformity or defect, is one-fifth of the wergild of the thumb, being thirty-three Dinars and one-third of a Dinar, when its setting is even and firm; and the wergild of its cracking is twenty-six Dinars and two-thirds of a Dinar; and the wergild for its exposure is eight Dinars and one-third of a Dinar; and the wergild of the displacement of its bone is sixteen Dinars and two-thirds of a Dinar; and the wergild for its piercing is eight Dinars and one-third of a Dinar, being half the wergild of the displacement of its bones.

And the wergild of its exposure is half the wergild of its displacement, being eight Dinars and one-third of a Dinar; and the wergild of it being disjointed is ten Dinars; and the wergild of the second joint from the top of the thumb, if it breaks and is set without deformity or defect, is sixteen Dinars and two-thirds of a Dinar; and the wergild of the exposure, if it is in it, is four Dinars and one-sixth of a Dinar; and the wergild of its cracking is thirteen Dinars and one-third of a Dinar; and the wergild of the displacement of its bones is five Dinars. So whatever is cut from it, it is by its accounting.
ai.seo_question: What is the financial compensation for breaking or cutting the thumb in Shia Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This passage from *Al-Kafi* provides a granular breakdown of *diyah* (blood money) for the hand (*al-kaff*) and thumb (*al-ibham*), reflecting the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on precise quantification of bodily injuries. It distinguishes compensation based on whether the injury heals without defect (*ghayr 'athm*) or with a lasting flaw (*'athm*), a key criterion in Shia *fiqh* for determining the value of permanent disability versus temporary injury.
